name: OSAllocatedUnfairLock (os framework)
verdict_reason: The underlying os_unfair_lock is about 1.4x faster than pthread_mutex (which NSLock wraps) when uncontended, but the one published contended test found OSAllocatedUnfairLock 1.75x slower than NSLock. The win holds for uncontended access only.
tier_reason: Independent forum measurement with the workload described, but no hardware, build settings or code for the timed variant.
claimed_speedup: Under contention it was slower: ~3.5 s vs ~2 s for NSLock (1.75x slower, derived from page data) for 100M increments from 10 parallel tasks; uncontended, the underlying os_unfair_lock took 0.12 s vs 0.172 s for pthread_mutex over 10 million cycles (1.4x faster, derived, 2019)
workload: 10 tasks in parallel, each incrementing one shared Int 10 million times (100M increments in total) behind NSLock, OSAllocatedUnfairLock, an atomic, or an actor; a single-thread run of the same work took about 0.1 s
one_liner: Heap-allocated Swift wrapper for os_unfair_lock; faster than NSLock uncontended, but measured 1.75x slower under heavy contention.
how_it_is_fast: It allocates the os_unfair_lock (and optionally the protected state) on the heap, so the lock has the stable address that a Swift value type cannot guarantee. Acquisition is an atomic compare-and-swap in user space, with a kernel call only on contention. The thread that measured it slower than NSLock under contention did not explain the cause.
use_it_when: Mostly uncontended locking on iOS 16+ / macOS 13+ where Mutex (iOS 18+) is not yet available
You need the os_unfair_lock speed without the unsafe &lock pattern
skip_it_when: Many threads hammer the same lock continuously; in the only published test NSLock finished faster
caveats: The poster said the OSAllocatedUnfairLock timing was unstable, between 3 and 4 seconds
Hardware, OS and build configuration are not stated for the contended test
The uncontended comparison is indirect: it measures raw os_unfair_lock against pthread_mutex in 2019, not OSAllocatedUnfairLock against NSLock
tradeoffs: One extra heap allocation per lock compared with Mutex

evidence.quote: I ran a simple loop, 10 million times, entering a mutex, incrementing a counter, and leaving the mutex.
